newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power moves up on cooler forecast, gas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power moves up on cooler forecast, gas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) moved higher Monday with strength from higher natural gas prices and forecasts of below normal temperatures, industry sources said.
"Gas prices are up for tomorrow, and we're expecting things to cool off quite a bit this week," said one ERCOT power trader.

Texas spot gas prices were said to have surged strongly by about $1.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) on Monday to about $3.35-3.40 per mmBtu. NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures were also trading up about 54 cents at near $3.65 per mmBtu.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday was talked in a $36.00-40.00 range early Monday afternoon, up from 25.00-$30.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) late last week, brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Tuesday's heavy load hours was notationally assessed higher at $34.00-38.00 per MWh in thin trade from $23.00-$29.00 on Friday, the sources said.

Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Tuesday were valued steady near $20.00, while non-firm delivery during Tuesday's light load hours was pegged at $15.00-18.00 from $19.00 late last week, the sources said.
February ERCOT power was valued $32.50-33.50 from $27.00-$28.00 late last week.
Temperatures in Texas were expected to cool from some summer-like weekend warmth, with highs expected Wednesday at near freezing through much of the state.
Longer term forecasts called for much-below normal temperatures through the western half of Texas from January 9 to 13, with the eastern half of Texas seen below normal during the same period.

Separately, Texas Utilities said Monday its 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 was expected to resume electricity production Tuesday or Wednesday after shutting over the weekend for the repair of a main feedwater valve.
